strings.name: Thasunda Brown Duckett
strings.summary: Thasunda Brown Duckett moved from housing, auto and consumer finance at Fannie Mae and JPMorgan Chase into retirement finance, becoming TIAA's president and CEO in 2021. She focuses on retirement saving and access to financial services and supports communities through a foundation named for her parents.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Only the filing-confirmed birth year, 1973, is retained. JPMorgan divisional CEO roles are distinguished from group CEO, temporary business oversight from permanent appointment, and event dates from report dates.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads TIAA's retirement savings and insurance business, participating in U.S. long-term saving, financial inclusion and institutional investment.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: BBA from the University of Houston in 1996, studying finance and marketing; MBA through Baylor University's Executive MBA program in 2001.
strings.facts.f2.label: Community philanthropy
strings.facts.f2.value: Founded the Otis and Rosie Brown Foundation, named for her parents, to support people contributing to their communities.
strings.highlights.h1.title: From consumer finance to retirement security
strings.highlights.h1.text: Led Chase's auto finance and consumer banking businesses before becoming TIAA president and CEO.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Financial inclusion and leadership
strings.highlights.h2.text: Publicly discusses retirement preparation, financial literacy and leadership; these initiatives do not establish that savings gaps have been eliminated.
strings.timeline.t1.title: ChiefX conversation report published
strings.timeline.t1.text: The organizer recapped her New York conversation with Alison Moore on leadership and financial security; this is the report date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Temporary oversight of retirement solutions
strings.timeline.t2.text: Media quoted a TIAA spokesperson saying she was overseeing the business after Kourtney Gibson's departure, pending a successor.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences
strings.timeline.t3.text: Elected in business, corporate and philanthropic leadership; this is not a scientific research degree.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes TIAA president and CEO
strings.timeline.t4.text: Succeeded Roger Ferguson as the appointment took effect.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Leads Chase Consumer Banking
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became CEO of the consumer banking business until moving to TIAA in 2021; not CEO of JPMorgan Chase as a whole.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Leads Chase Auto Finance
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became CEO of the auto finance business, serving until 2016.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earns Baylor MBA
strings.timeline.t7.text: Received a Master of Business Administration through the Executive MBA program.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduates and joins Fannie Mae
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned her University of Houston BBA and began working at Fannie Mae that year, later becoming a director of emerging markets.
